pg008_read0004: Acting is a powerful tool in the performing arts, capable of conveying important messages to audiences for the purpose of inspiring change in society. In this chapter, you will learn about the concept of drama and acting, and types of acting. The competencies developed will enable you to act skillfully while following the principles of acting.
pg008_read0006: How to act using actions with voice and mime
pg008_read0008: Drama and acting are very important concepts in the performing arts as they play a major role in conveying messages to the intended audience. Therefore, developing an insight into these concepts is essential in building skills in the field of acting.
pg008_read0009: Drama is a type of performing art that aims to convey a message to a live audience. In a drama performance, both the audience and the actor are present in the same place at the same time. In other forms of performing arts, such as music and film, this simultaneous presence of the two groups does not occur, or it is not necessary.
pg008_read0010: There are two types of drama performed on stage. The first type is written scripts, and the second type is improvised drama. The scripted drama differs from improvised drama because it requires long time to study and memorise the lines; while improvised drama depends on creativity of the actors.
pg009_read0001: Acting is a way of conveying a message to the audience through actions and word. Also, it is recognised as a career that requires the performer to be creative in conveying the message to the intended audience. The main performers are human beings who use their bodies and voices in a play to convey the message to the audience in a way that is engaging and easy to understand. Performers are required to be creative in various areas, including:
pg009_read0003: Using the body and voice creatively and skilfully;
pg009_read0005: Learn the audience and create the message according to their culture, interests and needs;
pg009_read0007: Selecting costumes that are in line with the theme; and
pg009_read0009: Preparing a performance space that aligns with the theme.
pg009_read0010: Four people sit around a table and talk together.
pg009_read0012: Prepare a performance that reflects the culture, interests and needs of any of the following groups: children, elderly people, workers or youth. Create a short play that appeals to the selected audience. Perform a play then explain how you created the content to fit their specific audience’s interests, culture, and needs.

pg009_read0021: There are various types of acting, such as acting with actions and voice, mime, image theatre and dance-drama. In this level, you will learn about acting with actions and voice, and acting without voice, commonly known as mime.
pg010_read0002: This is a type of acting that involves the use of words and actions to convey a message to the audience. A successful performance relies on the actor’s ability to balance actions and voice. Figure 1 presents pupils performing on a stage.

pg010_read0006: Aspects to consider when acting with actions and voice
pg010_read0007: Acting that involves both actions and voice requires careful attention and thorough preparation. The following are some important aspects to consider in this type of acting:
pg010_read0009: Understanding the character you are portraying.
pg010_read0010: It is essential to understand the character’s personality, background and goals. Additionally, develop an awareness of the character’s emotions in each scene and how they can be expressed through actions and voice. It is important to know how the character walks, speaks and struggles to achieve their objectives.
pg010_read0012: Mastering the use of body language.
pg010_read0013: Ensure that your body movements match the emotions you are intending to portray. Your movements must be purposeful. Avoid unnecessary movements on stage. Use your hands and facial expressions to convey different emotions such as happiness, sadness, surprise, or anger, rather than relying on words only.
pg011_read0003: To perform effectively on stage, control your voice by adjusting tone, speed and volume according to the context in reflecting the character’s emotions. Ensure that your voice and pronunciation are clear and audible to the audience.
pg011_read0006: Make sure you portray the character you are acting realistically. Avoid repetitive habits or uses of the same emotions in each scene.
pg011_read0009: Make sure that you listen and respond appropriately to the conversation initiated by your fellow performers during rehearsals. Make an attempt of maintaining good communication with them as you perform on stage in front of the audience.
pg011_read0012: To perform well on stage, make sure you are confident and seen by your audience. Learn to manage the stage. Do not stay in one area for the entire time of your performance on stage. Engage the audience through your creative use of body and voice while acting.
pg011_read0014: Practise regularly to improve your voice and appearance on stage.
pg011_read0015: Develop a habit of improving your acting skills. Read scripts of plays or watch films that showcase stage performances and imitate the characters using your gestures and voice.
pg011_read0018: The actor should make sure that the voice and actions match. For example, a performer portraying sadness should not use a strong voice or presents signs of excitement while on stage.

pg014_read0002: It is a form of performing arts in which performers use actions without words to convey a message to the audience. It is a powerful type of acting that relies entirely on body language, such as gestures, posture, and facial expressions, to convey messages without using words. The origin of mime can be traced back to early human history when the first human beings began to struggle with their lives. They used body language to communicate at a time when spoken language had not yet been discovered. For this reason, body language is considered an ancient form of communication that human beings used in the earliest stages of interaction.
pg014_read0003: As a form of performing arts, mime became popular in the 20
pg014_read0005: century. It was widely used in theatre and became a key element in early films, before the invention of sound technology. These early silent films relied completely on the actors’ ability to express themselves through mime to tell stories and engage viewers emotionally. Despite the advancements of technology and the development of sound in media, mime continues to hold an important place in both film and theatre. It is still used today in stage performances, movies and other forms of artistic expression. Mime also goes beyond the stage. People use gestures and body language in everyday situations to communicate when words are not available or necessary. Figure 2 shows the pupils performing a mime.

pg015_read0009: Mime depends on the body to convey messages. This means performers must develop skills to use their body parts to communicate with the audience without relying on words. This type of acting incorporates key elements such as body movements, music, emotions, facial expressions, symbols, sound effects and pantomime to convey a message. Examples of pantomimic movements include closing an imaginary door or holding an imaginary cup. All pantomime performances are accompanied by music or narration. These terms are very important in the field of acting. Therefore, building an understanding of their meanings and uses is crucial for the success of this type of acting. The terms are key factors to consider when performers use mime to convey a message to the audience.
pg015_read0010: Important things to consider in mime
pg015_read0011: There are several important aspects to consider in mime, including:
pg015_read0014: The body is the primary tool in mime. It is used to express thoughts and emotions using the body to reflect the intended message to the audience through the character you are portraying.
pg015_read0017: Use your body to express the emotions of your character, such as confidence, sadness, anxiety, or joy. For example, you might jump or laugh to show great happiness.
pg015_read0020: The face is an important part of showing various emotions because it has many muscles that can be used to express different emotions such as happiness, sadness, anger, fear or surprise. Ensure that the facial expressions you display are clear and easily visible to the audience.
pg015_read0023: Make sure actions involving invisible objects are realistic by considering their size, weight, and direction. This includes using body movements, posture, and gestures when interacting with imaginary objects, such as opening a door, carrying a heavy load, or holding a light ball.
pg016_read0003: Ensure that the pace of your acting movements matches the scene’s context. For example, if you act as if you are climbing a steep mountain, do not walk at a normal pace as if you are on flat ground.
pg016_read0006: Maintain eye contact with the audience to keep them involved in the performance. Body postures and positioning in facing the audience are the main tools that will help you ensure your audience is watching and following the performance. Develop the skill to communicate with your audience using your eyes.
pg016_read0008: Organisation and flow of the performance.
pg016_read0009: Ensure the performance has a smooth and logical flow from beginning to end. The sequence should be easy to follow, even without sound or words.
pg016_read0012: Mime requires physical strength and flexibility. Regular stage exercises can help improve body movements and performance.
pg016_read0014: Use of music and sound effects.
pg016_read0015: In mime, music and sound effects can be used to enhance emotions and guide the story. They help the audience understand the scene more effectively.
pg016_read0017: This art form plays a significant role in society and the world of performing arts. Some of its benefits include:
pg016_read0019: Promoting the traditions and customs of the nation both locally and internationally;
pg016_read0021: Helping actors and others understand how to use their bodies to convey messages effectively;
pg016_read0023: Fostering creativity as it requires significant creativity to express emotions and events through body movements and gestures;
pg016_read0025: Serving as a teaching tool, especially for children and people with hearing impairments;
pg016_read0027: Entertaining as it is a unique and captivating form of performing art;
pg016_read0029: Touching deeply the emotions of the audience because it compels people to understand the message by observing gestures and movements only; and
pg016_read0031: Developing acting talent in mime,whereas actors learn to channel their emotions without relying on words. This makes them better performers in other forms of acting.

pg017_read0011: Mime requires a long time of practise and rehearsal to convey a message to the audience;
pg017_read0013: Limited understanding of the audience, as not everyone has the ability to interpret performances that do not use words to convey the message, making some messages not easily understood;
pg017_read0014: Despite these challenges, mime as a form of acting remains an important art form that requires patience, creativity and dedication to make it more engaging and effective.

pg019_read0006: How musical dynamics and vocal balance improve singing
pg019_read0008: Musical dynamics involve changes in the level of the volume during singing or playing a musical instrument. These changes involve increasing or decreasing the volume. It is important for a singer or an instrumentalist to know when to increase the volume and when to decrease it. This helps to convey a message and make the emotion of the song clearer. Often, lowering the volume is one of the ways of achieving a soft or gentle sound. Music dynamics help a listener to understand and feel the emotions expressed through the song. There are terms and signs used to represent dynamics in a song. These terms and signs include:
pg019_read0011: This directs to sing or play an instrument softly. It is often used when singing or playing an instrument in a calm manner.
pg019_read0014: This directs to sing or play an instrument at a moderately soft but with gentleness. It is used when singing or playing an instrument in a calm manner with slight emphasis.
pg020_read0003: This directs to sing or play an instrument very softly. It is used when singing or playing an instrument in a state of great calmness or with an exceptionally gentle expression.
pg020_read0006: This directs to sing or play an instrument loudly. It is often used when singing or playing an instrument in situations of excitement or great emphasis.
pg020_read0009: This directs to sing or play an instrument moderately loud. It is used when singing or playing an instrument in situations that require moderate emphasis.
pg020_read0012: This directs to sing or play an instrument at a very loud and powerful volume. It is used when singing or playing an instrument in situations that require a strong impact or intensity.
pg020_read0015: This directs to sing or play an instrument, gradually increasing volume. It is used when singing or playing an instrument with greater emphasis on voice. Crescendo is represented using this symbol
pg020_read0018: This directs to sing or play an instrument, gradually decreasing the volume. It is used when singing or playing an instrument in a situation that requires a gradual reduction in voice intensity or excitement. Decrescendo is represented using this symbol
pg020_read0020: In music, particularly group singing, it is essential to have an understanding of musical dynamics in order to:
pg020_read0022: Enhance the beauty and appeal of the song.
pg020_read0023: Vocal variations in intensity between soft and loud make the song more exciting.
pg020_read0025: Effectively convey the message and emotions of the song.
pg020_read0026: Vocal rising and falling in a song create an emotion and help listeners understand the song thoroughly.
pg020_read0028: Add variety and avoid monotonous singing.
pg020_read0029: Variation in vocal intensity makes the singing lively and interesting.

pg029_read0012: Drawing involves how the artist creates and uses shapes to convey ideas, feelings, or stories through art. In the drawing, shapes are used to create structure, proportion, and balance in the image.
pg030_read0001: Principles of using shapes in drawing various objects
pg030_read0002: Using shapes in drawing is a basic method that helps create accurate and well-structured drawings. The following are important techniques to consider when using shapes in drawing:
pg030_read0004: Use circles to start drawing parts of circular shapes, such as a head, a wheel, or parts of flowers;
pg030_read0006: Use rectangles to show parts of objects with long sides, such as buildings, doors, or books;
pg030_read0008: Use four or three-sided shapes to create objects with triangular and rectangular proportions, such as windows or boxes;
pg030_read0010: Draw several shapes together to create a complex drawing. For example, connect circles and rectangles to create the body of a human being, animal, bird, or car;
pg030_read0012: Observe the size of the shape and space within to show the proportion of the object you are drawing;
pg030_read0014: Use sketch lines to get a map of the real image before drawing it, then draw the real image following those lines; and
pg030_read0016: Add shadows to the shapes in order to acquire depth and realism of the image.
pg030_read0018: Drawing using a circular shape is very important in artwork. This is because the circle is used as a basic part to draw other shapes, such as a mouth, head, or wheel. pg050_read0008: Flowerpots are containers used to keep flowers. These pots can be made using clay or cement. Cement pots are placed in a special place for a while to dry, then carved and finally filled with flowers. Clay pots must be dried and finally fired to make them stronger. Pots can be made by using pinching, coiling, slab, wheel throwing, and moulding techniques.
pg050_read0010: This is a method used to model pots by using a moulding technique. You must first prepare a mould of the shape you prefer to make. A mould is a tool that is made first to give shape to other vessels by the casting method. The caster presses the soft clay into the mould and stays there for a while until it dries, and then it is removed, having already copied the shape of the mould. By using a mould, you get the advantage of moulding many similar objects in a short time. Figure 1 shows an example of a mould ready to be used.

Other materials include thin wood, dry leaves, matches, cotton cloth, a small brush, a small knife, oil paints, kerosene, paint containers, a spade, a trowel and a plastic bucket or thick nylon and light nylon bags.

pg058_read0006: Flowerpots made of clay must be fired to make them strong. The fired flowerpots are resistant to erosion, even when saturated with water. The firing of these pots occurs in an open kiln, which differs from an interior kiln. An interior kiln is a small building equipped with a door for passing pots and air, as well as a designated firing area and a smoke tunnel. In contrast, an open kiln is simply a designated outdoor space where thin pieces of firewood and dry leaves are arranged in a slight pit to start the firing process. The key to effective firing is maintaining constant heating, which is why firewood and dry leaves are preferred materials.

pg058_read0014: Carefully arrange the clay pots that you want to fire on top of the layer of dry grass and firewood;
pg058_read0016: Add another layer of dry leaves and additional firewood to cover the pots completely. Once ready, light the fire to begin the firing process. Figure 10 shows that arrangement.

pg089_read0008: Football is a two-team sport played with the aim of scoring goals in the opponents’ goal. Each team has 11 players, including the goalkeeper. pg091_read0003: Passing is the intentional kicking or heading the ball from one player to another of the same team. This is a basic skill of the ball exchange between players of the same team to increase opportunities for attacking or defending. Accurate passing is essential for a team to be able to make quick attacks and reduce the opponent’s chances of winning the ball. Players need to know the time and distance required for each pass, and also have good communication to reduce mistakes. There are two main types of passes: short passes and long passes.
pg091_read0005: A short pass is the kicking or heading of the ball to a teammate who is at a short distance. Normally, this pass is made with the inside of the foot, as shown in Figure 2.

pg100_read0002: To be able to play netball well, a player must have the basic skills of the game. The essential netball skills include passing, catching, movements, shooting and defending.
pg100_read0005: Passing is the act of throwing the ball from one player to another of the same team. Passing accurately is essential for a team to attack quickly and prevent opponents from gaining possession of the ball. The main types of passes are chest pass, bounce pass and high pass.
pg100_read0007: A chest pass is the throwing of the ball, released from the passer’s chest, directly to the teammate’s chest using both hands. The pass is normally quick, easy and accurate to short distances. To be successful, the player must hold the ball with both hands and place it in front of the chest, then push it powerfully and accurately towards the teammate, as shown in Figure 10.

pg101_read0002: A bounce pass is the passing of the ball whereby the ball is thrown so as to bounce once before it reaches the receiving player. The ball is held with two hands while directing it to the bouncing point and released at an angle to bounce hard towards the teammate. This type of pass prevents the opponent from catching it as the ball is strategically directed to a teammate. It is often done for a short distance, as shown in Figure 11.

pg101_read0009: A high pass is the passing of the ball from the top of one player’s head to another player at a distance. This pass is often used when a player needs to deliver the ball over a long distance or when they want the ball to go over the obstacles of the opposing team. To make this pass, the player stands upright, takes the ball with both hands behind the head, and then pushes it forward with force and accuracy to reach the distant player, as shown in Figure 12.

pg107_read0020: To become a good netball player, it is important to ensure the following strategies:
pg107_read0023: A player should practice regularly to strengthen their playing skills, such as passing, receiving passes, and shooting. These exercises help improve the accuracy and speed of passing, as well as the ability to receive the ball without dropping it.
pg107_read0025: Participating in trial matches at school or out of school:
pg107_read0026: Participating in trial matches is an excellent way to learn by doing. These matches enhance the experience of playing as a team, help players understand each other’s tactics, and improve communication between them. It also helps to increase confidence and strengthen the ability to make quick decisions during the game.
pg107_read0028: Watching netball matches to help learning new techniques:
pg107_read0029: A player can learn better techniques by watching experienced players through live matches or videos. Watching top-level games helps to understand various techniques such as fast passing, effective tackling, and better
pg108_read0001: scoring opportunities. Moreover, learning new techniques from top players can improve the level of play and increase knowledge of the game.
pg108_read0003: Doing physical exercises like running and jumping:
pg108_read0004: Physical exercises are important for every netball player as they increase stamina, speed, and strength. Running helps to improve the ability to move quickly on the court, while jumping exercises strengthen the ability to jump high when scoring or catching the ball. These exercises also help to strengthen muscles and reduce the possibility of injuries during the game.

pg108_read0011: Netball is a fast-paced game that requires good cooperation between players to achieve victory. Apart from being a recreational game, netball provides many benefits to the individual player and society as a whole. The following are some of the important benefits of playing netball:
pg108_read0014: Playing netball is one of the best ways to improve physical well-being. This game involves many movements such as running, jumping, and passing the ball, which increase muscle strength, speed, and physical endurance. It also helps to improve the heart and lungs, lose weight, and improve blood circulation, thus reducing the risk of non-communicable diseases such as blood pressure and diabetes.
pg108_read0016: Builds cooperation and friendship between players.
pg108_read0017: Netball is a team game that requires good communication and cooperation between players. Through practice and matches, players learn to help each other, understand each other, and cooperate with the aim of winning the game. This cooperation increases solidarity and everlasting friendships even outside the field of play.
pg109_read0002: It helps to enhance discipline and quick decision-making.
pg109_read0003: Netball players learn to follow the rules of the game and respect the decisions of the referees, which builds discipline and good character. Hence, this game requires making quick decisions, such as passing the ball to a player in a good position or determining the right tackle. This strengthens the ability to think quickly and make the right decisions, not only on the field but also in everyday life.
pg109_read0005: It is a job opportunity for players who participate in major competitions.
pg109_read0006: For players with great talent and hard work, netball can be a source of employment. Players who can participate in major competitions at the national and international levels get the opportunity to play in major leagues and even get scholarships or work contracts. It can also open up other opportunities, such as becoming referees, coaches, or trainers of netball.
